bull.b: Sustained, rapid product revenue growth and expanding treatment-center adoption indicate durable commercial demand and rising physician acceptance. This supports higher recurring revenue, better utilization of manufacturing capacity, and strengthens the foundation for scaling into new geographies and indications over the next 2–6 months.

bull.t: Improving gross margins and unit economics
bull.b: A material shift to positive gross profit and planned manufacturing efficiencies point to improving unit economics. If sustained, margin expansion reduces per-treatment cash burn, enables reinvestment into commercialization, and makes peak ALL gross margins of ~65%–70% a realistic structural target supporting long-term profitability prospects.

bull.t: Extended funding capacity via new credit facility
bull.b: The senior credit facility materially extends runway and funds development and commercial scale-up milestones. Access to staged tranches tied to revenue milestones provides structural liquidity to pursue launches and trials, reducing immediate dilution risk and supporting execution on clinical and commercial plans over the medium term.

bear.b: Large negative operating and free cash flows demonstrate the company remains a cash-intensive developer and early commercializer. Persistent burn requires continued access to external capital or milestone-driven tranches, keeping dilution and refinancing risk elevated and constraining long-term financial flexibility if revenue cadence slows.

Even with an improving ALL franchise, rising SG&A for commercialization and reinvestment choices mean the company may remain loss-making at the corporate level. This uncertainty affects long-term returns and heightens sensitivity to execution, commercial uptake, and decisions on R&D or geographic expansion over the next several years.

bear.t: Manufacturing scale-up and market-access execution risk
bear.b: Growth into higher-volume indications and broader geographies depends on successful tech transfer and manufacturing scale-up plus market-access in Europe. Failure or delays would constrain supply, raise per-unit costs, and slow revenue and margin improvement, posing a structural execution risk to the company’s multi-indication expansion plans.
